passage: Many students study vocabulary by rereading their notes, but some teachers recommend self-quizzing instead. A researcher hypothesizes that students remember new vocabulary better when they test themselves than when they reread their notes.
stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the researcher's hypothesis?
choices: Students who spent 20 minutes quizzing themselves recalled more words a week later than students who spent 20 minutes rereading their notes.
Most students who took part in the study said that they prefer rereading their notes to quizzing themselves when they study new words.
Students who spent 20 minutes rereading their notes said afterward that they felt more confident about the words than students who quizzed themselves.
Both groups of students in the study spent the same amount of time studying the same list of 40 new vocabulary words.
steps: The hypothesis compares two methods by how well students remember.
The best support measures memory for both methods under fair conditions (same time).
Only the choice reporting recall a week later does that, and self-testing wins.
The other choices measure preferences or confidence, or describe the setup without giving a result.
key: Strong support measures the outcome named in the hypothesis and compares the groups fairly.
source: SAT AIS original item, written to the College Board Digital SAT content specifications
